notes: QAT: qcb.gov.qa and almeezan.qa returned no usable URL from search; the Qatar Central Bank Law (Law No. 13 of 2012, 238 articles) is described in words by Gulf Times, which states the bank is under the direct control of the Emir, the Governor is appointed by Emiri decision, and the board seats representatives of the Ministries of Economy and Finance and of Business and Trade. The Clifford Chance briefing (cliffordchance.com, Feb 2013, fetched) confirms Law 13/2012 was enacted and replaced Law 33/2006 but says nothing about executive control, so the Gulf Times report is the source. Law 13/2012 is still the governing QCB law. SAU: filed from SAMA's own rulebook, which marks the Saudi Central Bank Law (M/36, 26/11/2020) as 'In-Force' - Article 2 (reports to the King) and Article 8 (board appointed by royal order on the joint nomination of the Governor and the Minister of Finance); the same page's footnotes show the Council of Ministers amending Article 11 by Resolution No. 412. SGP: mas.gov.sg was down for the whole run ('service is currently unavailable', maintenance page) and sso.agc.gov.sg serves the MAS Act only through JavaScript, so the board route was used: MAS's own 3 July 2023 announcement, reproduced verbatim on Mondo Visione, names the Deputy PM and Minister for Finance as Board Chairman and the Minister for Trade and Industry as Deputy Chairman; marked weak_source because the text is a mirror of the MAS release, not mas.gov.sg itself. Worth a hand check: https://www.mas.gov.sg/who-we-are/board-of-directors to confirm a serving minister still chairs. CRI: filed on three serving cabinet ministers writing to the BCCR president to demand a change of exchange-rate policy, with the President endorsing it at a press conference. MDV: filed on the Majlis suspending Article 32(a)(b)(e) of the Fiscal Responsibility Act to let the Finance Ministry overdraw the MMA. BIH: two records - the Council of Ministers earmarking CBBH profit for an arbitration debt (bank suspended the transfer), and the Presidency sacking two of five Governing Board members in June 2019 (centralbanking.com lede is free; the body is paywalled, so the record states only what the free text says). SYR: the Transitional Presidency replaced the sitting governor by Decree No. 99 of 2026; filed as a replacement by decree, not as an appointment controversy. RULED OUT / EVIDENCE STOPPED: MAC - both gazette hosts (bo.io.gov.mo and images.io.gov.mo) return CONNECT 502 through the proxy and amcm.gov.mo is a JavaScript-only shell, so Decreto-Lei 14/96/M could not be read; needs a hand check of https://bo.io.gov.mo/bo/i/96/13/declei14.asp. TJK - dif.tj (which hosts the Russian text of the Law on the National Bank of Tajikistan at https://dif.tj/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Zakon-RT-o-NBT.pdf) reset the connection mid-transfer, WIPO Lex text 498558 renders only through JavaScript, and base.spinform.ru returned an empty page; the law was never read, so nothing filed. LTU - the only ECB-opinion lead found was on the bank solidarity levy on commercial banks (lrt.lt), which is a tax on banks, not an act against Lietuvos bankas; no CON opinion on Lietuvos bankas's own statute surfaced. MLT - searches returned ECB opinions for Cyprus, Croatia, Slovenia, Spain and Ireland but none on the Central Bank of Malta; nothing read, nothing filed. SMR - the only hits were the Consiglio Grande e Generale's own document index pages with no readable titles, so no dated act on Banca Centrale di San Marino was found.

records.kind: statutory arrangement placing the bank under the head of state
records.summary: The Emir issued Law No. 13 of 2012 on the Qatar Central Bank and the Regulation of Financial Institutions, 238 articles, under which the QCB, although a corporate body with its own budget, is placed under the direct control of the Emir, its Governor is appointed by Emiri decision for a five-year renewable term with the rank of a minister, and its board of directors seats representatives of the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Ministry of Business and Trade. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
records.source_title: New law regulating Qatar Central Bank - Gulf Times

records.kind: statutory arrangement subordinating the bank to the King and the finance ministry
records.summary: The Saudi Central Bank Law, issued by Royal Decree No. M/36 of 26 November 2020 and marked In-Force in the bank's own rulebook, provides in Article 2 that the Bank is a legal person which reports to the King, and in Article 8(2) that the five non-government members of its board are nominated jointly by the Governor and the Minister of Finance and appointed by royal order, with their pay set by royal order on the Minister of Finance's recommendation; the published footnotes to Article 11 record the Council of Ministers amending the Law by Resolution No. 412. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
records.source_title: Saudi Central Bank Law, Chapter 2: Management - SAMA Rulebook

records.kind: statutory arrangement placing serving cabinet ministers in charge of the bank's board
records.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore announced on 3 July 2023 that the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance would be appointed Chairman of the MAS Board of Directors from 8 July 2023, that the Minister for Trade and Industry would be appointed to the Board and made Deputy Chairman, and that the outgoing chairman had himself been a serving Senior Minister through twelve years in the post. The record rests on who the bank itself says sits on and chairs its board, a standing arrangement with no end date, because the MAS website and the statute database could not be read.
records.source_title: Appointment Of New Chairman And Deputy Chairman To Monetary Authority Of Singapore Board Of Directors (MAS release)

records.kind: ministers demand a change of exchange-rate policy in writing
records.summary: Three serving cabinet ministers of Costa Rica, the Minister of Foreign Trade, the Minister of Agriculture and the Minister of Tourism, sent three letters to the president of the Banco Central de Costa Rica, Roger Madrigal, demanding that the bank revise its exchange-rate policy because the colon's appreciation had reached a critical point for exporters and free-zone firms; President Rodrigo Chaves endorsed the approach at a press conference on 31 January 2024, saying the government had told the bank it wanted transitory currency movements not to cause permanent changes.
records.source_title: Chaves pide al Banco Central que se asegure de que comportamiento del dolar sea transitorio - El Observador CR

records.kind: parliament suspends fiscal law to let the government overdraw the central bank
records.summary: The People's Majlis approved the Finance Ministry's request to extend by a further year, to the end of 2023, the period in which the government may overdraw the public account held at the Maldives Monetary Authority, carried by 42 votes; parliament had earlier suspended Article 32(a)(b)(e) of the Fiscal Responsibility Act to allow MVR 4.4 billion to be overdrawn from the MMA, and the outstanding MVR 2.5 billion was to be converted into a 50-year amortisable bond issued by the MMA at a 2.5 percent coupon.
records.source_title: Parliament approves overdraft extension til end of 2023 - The Times of Addu

records.kind: government earmarks the bank's profit to pay a state debt
records.summary: The Council of Ministers of Bosnia and Herzegovina adopted a revised 2025 draft budget for state institutions that provided for the liabilities arising from the Viaduct v BiH international arbitration to be settled out of the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina's profits; the bank, whose Governing Board had allocated 244.3 million convertible marks of its 412.6 million marks of 2024 net profit for transfer to the Ministry of Finance and Treasury, publicly suspended that transfer, saying the use of the money for arbitration debt would endanger its assets and the country's financial stability.
records.source_title: Bosnia's Central Bank refuses budget transfer amid arbitration debt concerns - N1

records.kind: board members sacked by the head of state
records.summary: Two of the five members of the Governing Board of the Central Bank of Bosnia and Herzegovina were sacked by the country's tripartite Presidency, the collective head of state, in a move reported on 25 June 2019 whose stated reasons were unclear; both the Presidency and the central bank are governed by the ethnic power-sharing arrangements written into the Dayton peace settlement.
records.source_title: Bosnian central bank board members sacked by president - Central Banking

records.summary: Syria's transitional president, Ahmad al-Sharaa, issued Decree No. 99 of 2026 replacing the sitting governor of the Central Bank of Syria, Abdul Qader al-Hasriya, with Mohammed Safwat Raslan, roughly a year after al-Hasriya had himself been installed by presidential decree in April 2025; the change was announced through the state news agency SANA, the head of state acting alone on the leadership of the central bank.
records.source_title: Syrian president appoints Mohammed Safwat Raslan as central bank governor - North Press Agency
